rows.text: Under D.Lgs. 81/2008, art. 71, c. 11, INAIL must carry out the first periodic verification of Annex VII equipment within 45 days of the request. This prevails over the 60 days in DM 11 April 2011, art. 2, c. 1, because a D.Lgs. outranks a DM.

rows.text: Under art. 71, comma 2 of D.Lgs. 81/2008, when choosing work equipment the employer must consider the specific conditions and characteristics of the work, the risks in the work environment, the risks from using the equipment, and the risks from interference with other equipment already in use.

Yes. Under art. 72, c. 2 of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (DLGS72.md), the person renting out operator-less work equipment must, besides certifying its good condition, obtain and keep on file for the whole rental a self-certifying declaration attesting the specific training and instruction of the users.

rows.value: Persona competente: the initial, periodic and extraordinary checks under art. 71(8)(a) and (b) must be carried out by a competent person.
rows.text: Under art. 71, comma 8, letter (c), of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (DLGS71.md), the checks in letters (a) and (b), covering the initial, periodic and extraordinary checks, must be carried out by a competent person (persona competente); the employer must ensure this.
Under Annex VII, row 10 of Legislative Decree 81/2008, mast climbing work platforms (piattaforme di lavoro autosollevanti su colonne) require a biennial periodic verification, i.e. every two years.

Under DM 11 April 2011, Allegato III, punto 4.1, registration in the list of authorised bodies is valid for five years (quinquennale) and can be renewed by a specific application after a positive review of the renewal documents. (Worked out from the sentences cited: the period P5Y is not written in the sentences pointed at.)

rows.text: Under DM 11 April 2011, Allegato II, punto 3.1.2, the verifier of the first periodic verification of SC and SP equipment must examine the CE declaration of conformity, the declaration of correct installation (where legally required), load tables/diagrams (where provided), the work-area diagram (where provided), and the instructions for use.

No. Under DM 11 April 2011, Allegato I, point 4, an authorised body that carried out product certification may not perform the first periodic verification of the specific work equipment for which it issued the CE-marking certification.

According to the Global Service excerpt (Appendice A, Art. 16.2 'Cappe chimiche') in the University of Catania guideline on work equipment, p. 13, scheduled maintenance of chemical fume hoods is semiannual (every six months), excluding filter replacement, which is annual.

Yes. In the INAIL guide, section 7.1 (p. 44), when the manufacturer requests recognition and the prototype is examined at its premises, the recognition extends to the whole series, and the manufacturer then issues a conformity certificate for each unit to all users. The identity-check condition on p. 43 concerns only units already delivered.

rows.value: The RDRL (head of teaching or research activity in the laboratory where the instrument is located) decides, unless the employer (Datore di Lavoro) of the structure indicates otherwise.
rows.text: Per the UNIVPM laboratory equipment guidelines (company procedure, Ver. 1.0 – Marzo 2024), section 7.3 Modello C, the setting up of the usage register is decided by the RDRL of the laboratory where the equipment is located, except where the Datore di Lavoro of the structure directs otherwise.

Under Article 10(7) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG), as the Regulation applies from 20 January 2027 (Art. 54, as corrected), the manufacturer must provide paper instructions free of charge within one month of a user's request made at the time of purchase.

Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 13(8), importers must keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product has been placed on the market.

No. Under Article 15(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, a distributor with reason to believe the machinery does not conform must not make it available on the market until it is brought into conformity. Informing the manufacturer or importer and the market surveillance authorities is an additional duty, and the Regulation applies from 20 January 2027 (Article 54), before 1 March 2027.

rows.text: Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 25(2), for a category listed in Annex I, Part A (point 3, vehicle servicing lifts), the manufacturer may choose module B followed by module C, module H, or module G; the Regulation applies from 20 January 2027, so it governs a placement on 1 March 2027.
Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies in general from 20 January 2027 under Article 54 (second sentence, as corrected by Corrigendum point 10); the earlier dates in Article 54 (a)-(d) are exceptions.
Under Article 50(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum (point 4), Member States must notify the Commission of the penalty rules and measures by 20 October 2026.

No. Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the transitional permission covers only products placed on the market under Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027, and Article 51(2) repeals that Directive with effect from 20 January 2027, so a first placing on exactly that day must comply with the Regulation.

Yes. Under Article 10(8) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), the manufacturer may instead of accompanying the machine provide, in the instructions for use, the internet address or machine-readable code where the EU declaration of conformity can be accessed; the Regulation applies to machines placed on the market from 20 January 2027 (Art. 54, as corrected), so it governs a machine placed on the market on 1 March 2027.

The documents provided do not state the penalty for an employer who fails to subject Annex VII equipment to the periodic verifications of Article 71(11) of D.Lgs. 81/2008; Article 71(11) itself (DLGS71.md) sets out the verification obligation and costs but no fine, and the sanctions article is not in the files.

DLGS73, art. 73, comma 5 delegates the duration of the operator qualification course to a Conferenza permanente Stato-Regioni decision. The files contain no such decision, so the number of hours for telescopic handlers is not stated.

The folder references the general safety requirements of Allegato V of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (art. 70, c. 2), but does not contain the text of that annex, so the emergency stop requirements for machines built without product directives cannot be stated from these documents; the only 'emergency stop devices' item found is point 10 of Annex V to the Machinery Directive (DIR.md), which is a different instrument.

The files do not name a harmonised EN standard giving presumption of conformity for vehicle servicing lifts under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Article 20(1) refers only to standards published in the Official Journal); the regulation applies from 20 January 2027 per the Corrigendum, point 10.

The documents do not name the Italian national market surveillance authority for machinery. Article 70(4) of D.Lgs. 81/2008 refers only to the 'autorità nazionale di sorveglianza del mercato competente per tipo di prodotto' without naming it.

IGEA device 19 must be verified every P1Y on 2026-11-14: AUTOGRU is lifting equipment of type mobile o trasferibile (mapping of the rule); capacity 5000 kg is above 200 kg; sector estrattivo: named in the row; Annex VII row for type mobile, sector use (source: DLGSALLVII, Allegato VII, riga 12). Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, an elevating platform as a mobile elevating work platform (not verified on its manual), and the site's sector applies to every device unless the question states another use.

IGEA device 7 must be verified every P2Y on 2027-12-31: GRU IDRAULICA PER AUTOCARRO is lifting equipment of type mobile o trasferibile (mapping of the rule); capacity 790 kg is above 200 kg; sector regular use (stated in the question): regular use; built in 2017: not more than 10 years before 2027-12-31; Annex VII row for type mobile, regular use, age new. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, an elevating platform as a mobile elevating work platform (not verified on its manual), and the site's sector applies to every device unless the question states another use.

Per DLGSALLVII Allegato VII riga 16 (biennial) and riga 15 (annual), the crane (built 2017, extractive sector) switches from biennial to annual only when its manufacture year is older than 10 years, around 2027. The files give only the year 2017, so the exact day is not stated.

IGEA device 13 must be verified every P2Y on 2026-11-14: GRU A PONTE SCORREVOLE is lifting equipment of type fisso (mapping of the rule); capacity 5000 kg is above 200 kg; sector estrattivo: named in the row; built in 2017: not more than 10 years before 2026-11-14; Annex VII row for type fisso, sector use, age new (source: DLGSALLVII, Allegato VII, riga 16). Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, an elevating platform as a mobile elevating work platform (not verified on its manual), and the site's sector applies to every device unless the question states another use.

Under D.Lgs. 81/08 Allegato VII, riga 15, fixed lifting appliances over 200 kg used in extractive settings and built more than 10 years ago need annual checks. Yearly checks therefore apply to overhead cranes 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 and to gantry crane 23. Overhead crane 13 (built 2017) falls under riga 16 and is checked every two years.

In table A4 (Allegato A, igea-equipment.md, p. 7), the autogru positions with capacity above 5000 kg are 17 (P&H R200, 18760 kg), 18 (JCB JS190NLC, 7500 kg) and 21 (JCB JS190NLC, 7500 kg). The store's answer omits position 17.

2 of the 24 devices of the IGEA list satisfy position >= 1 and position <= 7 and kind in ['AUTOGRU', 'GRU IDRAULICA PER AUTOCARRO'] and capacity_kg < 1000 and year_built < 2005 on 2026-11-14: positions 5, 6. Worked out in code over the device facts.

Under DM 11 April 2011, Allegato II, point 5.2.1, the employer must request the competent ASL to carry out the verifications subsequent to the first at least 30 days before the expiry of the deadline (P30D).

Yes. Under the DM of 11 April 2011, Allegato II, point 5.3.3, the employer must notify the competent INAIL territorial office of the relocation of equipment for the database entry. The GUTTER crane is in the plant record as a sliding overhead crane (gru a ponte scorrevole) at Masua, position 10.

rows.value: The employer (datore di lavoro) bears the cost of the periodic verifications under Art. 71, comma 11, D.Lgs. 81/2008.
rows.text: Under Art. 71, comma 11 of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (DLGS71.md), the verifications are carried out for a fee and their costs are charged to the employer, so the employer pays for the periodic verifications of the IGEA lifting devices.

rows.text: Under point 4.2.2 of the IGEA technical sheet (igea-equipment, p. 4-5), for device 8 (DEMAG 1985, not CE-marked, over 20 years old) IGEA must provide the INAIL/ISPESL verification booklet, the previous periodic verification reports, the control register, and the structural verification certificate for remaining life cycles; the CE-only documents do not apply.
According to the MA STAR two-post lift manual, section 7.2.2 (page 31), the lubrication felt must be checked for wear and/or contamination and replaced at least every 12 months.

rows.value: The operator (the lift operator) is responsible for ensuring nobody is within the danger zone before lowering the vehicle.
rows.text: MA STAR manual, section 4.4.4 'Lowering Process' (p. 20): before lowering the vehicle, the operator is responsible for ensuring that nobody is within the danger zone.

According to the nanoScan3 manual, section 5.6.2 'Planning the regular thorough check' (page 50, and page 51 'Minimum requirements for the regular thorough check'), the regular thorough checks must be carried out at least once a year. (Worked out from the sentences cited: the period P1Y is not written in the sentences pointed at.)
The nanoScan3 operating instructions, section 2.3 Improper use (p. 11), list as impermissible use: use as a physical guard, access control or authorization, and detection of transparent items.
No. The UR5e manual, section 18.2 'Robot Arm Cleaning and Inspection' (Robot Arm Inspection NOTICE), says never to use compressed air to clean the robot arm because it can damage the components.
According to the UR5e user manual, section 17.4 Long Term Storage, a robot is considered long-term stored when it is stored for a period of 6 months or more.
No. The UR10e User Manual (p. 196, Risk Assessment) requires that after an emergency stop is activated it be manually reset at the push-button that initiated the stop.

According to the UR10e User Manual, section 19 'Disposal and Environment' (p. 224), the responsibility for disposing of the robot in accordance with national laws, regulations and standards rests with the owner of the robot.

The files do not state how many residual life cycles result from the structural verification certification of DEFRIES-TITANO crane at position 11. The IGEA plant record only requires that certification for equipment older than 20 years, and device 11 was built in 1978.

The documents do not state a penalty for an employer who fails to submit lifting equipment to the periodic verification under Article 71(11) of D.Lgs. 81/2008; Article 71(11) only imposes the duty and the sanctions provision is not in the files.
The files do not state the tightening torque for the HAS-U M16 anchor rods of the MA STAR columns; the manual (mastar-manual.md, pp. 9-10) names the anchor rod but gives no torque value.
The documents do not state an MTTFd value for the SICK nanoScan3; nanoscan3-manual gives only PL d, PFH and mission time TM (20 years) in its technical data.

The UR5e User Manual does not state the weight of the Control Box; its specification table (3.1, p. 18) gives only the robot arm weight of 20.7 kg / 45.7 lb, and section 5.2 says only that the Control Box can be carried by one person.
